Lesson 5 · EGE English

Revision → Present Perfect Continuous
Past Perfect → Future Continuous

Собираем уже изученные времена в одну систему, затем добавляем три новых. В чтении учимся выбирать ответ по конкретным доказательствам в тексте, а не по общему впечатлению.

01 · REVISION

Quick revision — выбери форму по контексту

Вспомни уже изученные времена. Обращай внимание на смысл, временные указатели и связь между действиями.

1. My sister usually ___ (read) before bed, but today she ___ (watch) a documentary.

2. We ___ (not / see) the exhibition last weekend because it ___ (be) closed.

3. At 8 p.m. yesterday, I ___ (do) my homework when my friend ___ (call).

4. “I can’t carry these bags.” — “I ___ (help) you.”

5. She ___ already ___ (write) the email, so you can send it.

6. ___ you ever ___ (try) food from another country?

Ключи: 1 reads; is watching. 2 didn’t see; was. 3 was doing; called. 4 will help. 5 has; written. 6 Have; tried.

Проверяем логику: usually → привычка; today → действие сейчас/временная ситуация; last weekend → завершённое прошлое; at 8 p.m. yesterday + when → процесс и короткое событие; предложение помочь → спонтанное решение; already/ever → Present Perfect.

02 · VERB REVIEW

Повторение неправильных глаголов

Вспомни три формы глагола: Infinitive — Past Simple — Past Participle (V₃). Они нужны для уже изученных времён и новых тем этого урока. Введи две недостающие формы через пробел, например: went gone.

1. go — ___ — ___

2. see — ___ — ___

3. write — ___ — ___

4. take — ___ — ___

5. speak — ___ — ___

6. begin — ___ — ___

7. choose — ___ — ___

8. forget — ___ — ___

9. know — ___ — ___

10. leave — ___ — ___

11. make — ___ — ___

12. give — ___ — ___

13. bring — ___ — ___

14. buy — ___ — ___

15. think — ___ — ___

Ключи:
1 go — went — gone
2 see — saw — seen
3 write — wrote — written
4 take — took — taken
5 speak — spoke — spoken
6 begin — began — begun
7 choose — chose — chosen
8 forget — forgot — forgotten
9 know — knew — known
10 leave — left — left
11 make — made — made
12 give — gave — given
13 bring — brought — brought
14 buy — bought — bought
15 think — thought — thought
02 · NEW

Present Perfect Continuous

Когда используем: действие началось в прошлом и продолжается до настоящего момента либо только что закончилось, а мы видим его результат. Важны длительность или сам процесс.

+
have / has + been + V-ing

I have been studying for two hours.

She has been working all morning.

−
haven’t / hasn’t + been + V-ing

He hasn’t been sleeping well.

?
Have / Has + subject + been + V-ing?

Have you been waiting long?

СигналКак понятьПример
for two hoursдлительность периодаThey have been talking for two hours.
since Mondayс какого момента началосьShe has been learning English since Monday.
all day / recentlyпроцесс длился долго или происходил в последнее времяI’m tired because I have been running.

Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous: Present Perfect часто подчёркивает результат/количество: I have written three emails. Present Perfect Continuous подчёркивает процесс/длительность: I have been writing emails for an hour.

7. Your eyes are red. ___ you ___ (cry)?

8. He ___ (work) on this project since March, and he still hasn’t finished.

9. I ___ (read) three chapters, so I can answer your questions now.

Ключи: 7 Have; been crying. 8 has been working. 9 have read. В №9 подчёркнут завершённый результат — три главы, поэтому Present Perfect.
03 · NEW

Past Perfect

Когда используем: действие произошло раньше другого момента или действия в прошлом. Past Perfect помогает показать, что было первым.

+
had + V₃

When we arrived, the film had started.

−
hadn’t + V₃

She hadn’t finished by 6.

?
Had + subject + V₃?

Had they left before you called?

Сравни: When I arrived, they were eating dinner. — я пришла, и они были в процессе. When I arrived, they had eaten dinner. — они уже поели до моего прихода.

Частые подсказки: by the time, already, before, after, when — но решает не само слово, а порядок событий.

10. By the time the bus arrived, we ___ (wait) for forty minutes. (Используй Past Perfect; не добавляй Continuous.)

11. When I got to the station, the train ___ already ___ (leave).

12. ___ you ___ (finish) the report before the meeting began?

Ключи: 10 had waited — в этом задании тренируем только Past Perfect. 11 had; left. 12 Had; finished. Логика: к моменту прибытия поезда уже не было; отчёт нужно было закончить до начала встречи.
04 · NEW

Future Continuous

Когда используем: действие будет происходить в процессе в конкретный момент в будущем. Представляем себя в будущем времени и спрашиваем: «Что будет происходить в этот момент?»

+
will be + V-ing

This time tomorrow, I will be flying to Bali.

−
won’t be + V-ing

At 8, she won’t be working.

?
Will + subject + be + V-ing?

Will you be using the laptop at 6?

Подсказки: this time tomorrow, at 7 p.m. next Friday, this time next week. Они указывают на момент, когда действие будет в процессе.

13. This time next week, we ___ (travel) around Japan.

14. ___ you ___ (work) at 9 tomorrow morning?

15. Don’t call at 7. I ___ (drive) home.

Ключи: 13 will be travelling / traveling. 14 Will; be working. 15 will be driving.
05 · EGE READING

Reading · задания 12–18: три текста

Прочитай каждый текст и выбери один из четырёх вариантов ответа. В Teacher version к каждому вопросу есть ключ, логика выбора и конкретное доказательство из текста. В самом тексте доказательства подсвечиваются в режиме преподавателя.

Алгоритм чтения: 1) прочитай вопрос и подчеркни, что именно спрашивают; 2) найди в тексте нужный абзац; 3) выдели подтверждающие слова; 4) проверь все варианты и исключи те, которые противоречат тексту, слишком широкие или вообще не упоминаются.

Variant 1 · Cross-cultural communication

Общение между культурами · источник: загруженный сборник, PDF: стр. 9–10

Communicating cross-culturally can be exciting and rewarding, but even wise and accomplished communicators often make some of the more common cross-cultural communication mistakes. Before you embark on your journey (or even if you’re midway down the road!), consider some useful tips. When it comes to communication, an ounce of prevention is truly worth a pound of cure.

First of all, assume good intentions. Every cross-cultural worker knows this moment: you're in discussion with an individual from another culture, when they say something totally offensive or rude. You're a bit taken aback and feel defensive. How could they say that? In this moment, especially if you feel tired from jet lag or overwhelmed with culture shock, it can be so easy to try to “correct” the individual or respond defensively, but doing so may damage the relationship and leave the other person confused.

It’s hard enough to guess intentions in your own culture, but cross-cultural guessing can be even trickier. It’s very possible the other person's words are based on some cultural frame of reference you don’t understand, or they simply mistranslated a word or phrase. Take a step back. Take a breath. Give them the benefit of the doubt.

Obviously, not all interactions come from good intentions. It can be helpful to run the interaction by a trusted individual from within the culture who can help you understand what you might have missed.

For the time being, however, you'll want to ask clarifying questions. You’re in the midst of an interaction and something comes off, either relationally or informationally. Maybe the person suggested a plan that appears completely outside of the parameters of your discussion with them. Maybe they said something that seemed to hold a sharp edge to it. Maybe you are just completely lost (it happens!).

Your best option is to ask a few questions to get some clarification. When shouldn’t you ask clarifying questions? If you’re a newbie to the culture and the other individual said something that feels like a personal attack, it’s best to get the discussion focused back on the main point, and then check in with a trusted local friend. For example, in certain Asian cultures it’s completely acceptable to say, “You've gotten a little fatter!” In fact, if you've been apart for a season and the speaker recognizes that you've gained weight, it shows attentiveness to you. Imagine the confusion if your counterpart thinks they are showing positive interest in you and you respond like a prickly cactus.

In cross-cultural communication, don’t rely fully on your intuition. The thing is: intuition isn’t some mysterious super-power you can pull out at will; rather it is a conglomerate of observational skills that are highly informed by the culture you grew up in and the accumulation of your past experiences. We’ve seen highly educated and intelligent individuals crash and burn when relying on their “gut” in cross-cultural interactions.

How do you remedy this situation? Research, research, research. Read books. Ask questions. Observe interactions between members of the host culture. Pay attention to positive and negative responses to your own interactions with the culture. By doing this you build up that weight of experience to inform your observations.

The reality is that you most probably will make mistakes. The good news, though, is that people often recognize the signs of a person who is genuinely seeking to understand and honour their culture. By becoming a student of the people you communicate with, you demonstrate a respect that at times will open more doors than a perfect presentation.

Questions 12–18

12. In paragraph 1, the author writes that cross-cultural communication is …

Ответ: 3. worth doing and quite interesting
Логика: “exciting and rewarding” прямо передаёт положительную оценку общения. Это соответствует варианту 3; остальные варианты не передают эту мысль.

13. According to the text, how can correcting an individual make them feel?

Ответ: 4. Confused
Логика: В абзаце 2 сказано: “...may damage the relationship and leave the other person confused.” Ключевое слово — confused.

14. Which is NOT mentioned in the text as a reasonable way to deal with seemingly rude behaviour?

Ответ: 2. Trying to guess the person's intentions
Логика: Автор советует не полагаться на догадки: “cross-cultural guessing can be even trickier”. Он предлагает сделать паузу и дать человеку benefit of the doubt. Поэтому именно попытка угадать намерения не является рекомендацией.

15. According to the text, asking clarifying questions can help …

Ответ: 4. if you lack understanding with a person
Логика: В абзаце 5 описана ситуация, когда смысл взаимодействия неясен: “You’re ... something comes off...” и “Maybe you are just completely lost.” Вопросы нужны для clarification.

16. What is the best strategy in case an individual makes personal remarks you find offensive, according to the author?

Ответ: 1. Concentrating on the subject
Логика: Автор уточняет исключение: если новичок в культуре воспринимает слова как личную атаку, лучше вернуть обсуждение к главной теме: “get the discussion focused back on the main point”. Это вариант 1.

17. The expression relying on their “gut” is closest in meaning to …

Ответ: 1. acting based on feelings
Логика: “Gut” здесь означает интуитивное чувство/внутреннее ощущение. Ближайший смысл — acting based on feelings. Автор при этом предупреждает, что одной интуиции недостаточно.

18. What is the main idea of the text as stated in the last paragraph?

Ответ: 2. Being polite and ready to learn is the main thing
Логика: Финальный абзац подчёркивает, что люди замечают искреннее желание понять и уважать культуру: “genuinely seeking to understand and honour their culture”. Это ближе всего к варианту 2.

Variant 2 · Happy holidays?

Праздники и чувство одиночества · источник: загруженный сборник, PDF: стр. 20–21

Thanksgiving is approaching and most Americans have solidified their family plans for the holiday. Whether you're hosting a big meal or heading to a relative's house, the holidays are often a chance to reconnect with loved ones. However, Thanksgiving Day isn’t always a family-oriented occasion.

Over the years, several studies have found that the seemingly joyous holiday season isn’t always easy for everyone. In one survey, 31 per cent of respondents said they felt lonely during the holidays throughout the last five years. Meanwhile, 41 per cent of participants were concerned about a family member or a friend feeling lonely around the holidays. Another survey also found that 70 per cent of respondents struggled with different types of loneliness before Thanksgiving and Christmas, partly due to the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic.

While socially-distanced holiday parties have mostly become a thing of the past since then, there are still many reasons why some people spend the season by themselves. Some have family members living on the opposite side of the country, or world, while others may not have a close relationship with their relatives at all.

There's no one concrete way to spend the holidays, and everyone has their own reasons why they choose not to see certain people on a festive day. A therapist, Lilia Magon, acknowledged that when we spend the holidays alone, our feelings of loneliness can be heightened. While everyone experiences loneliness in a different way, Magon believes that the feeling could be tied to how Thanksgiving has been portrayed over the years.

“I think a lot of the anxieties and concerns that come up have to do with unmet expectations of what you think a holiday is supposed to look like, and what you think your relationship with your family or your friends is supposed to look like,” she said. “I think that’s where a lot of people themselves feel a little bit of a stressful state. Just maybe feeling a little let down by the expectations they have for themselves, after watching other people experience the holidays differently than them.”

The holidays are often referred to as the most wonderful time of the year, but that doesn’t ring true for everyone. In some cases, the winter months can be quite a triggering time, and potentially a reminder to people of how they've been hurt by those closest to them. According to Magon, the best way to manage those feelings of animosity is by gaining perspective about the holidays and new ways to celebrate.

“I think you should allow yourself to reframe it as: ‘Okay, how do I want these days to look for me? Who are the people that I do want in my life? Who are the people that I don't want in my life?’” she advised. “Don’t try to make something happen that wouldn’t happen. Instead, recreate your own memories and your own traditions, and give yourself space and permission to do so. But also, if you know that it's going to be hard for you, create your own support system, by reaching out to a therapist or a trusted friend.”

For those who do have a close support system, it can make dropping in on Thanksgiving dinner a little easier. On the other hand, your cousins might be sitting next to you at the dinner table. Still, Magon believes we shouldn’t try to convince family members to attend an event in which they've already opted out. “If someone decides they don’t want to be with family during the holidays, respect that choice for them,” she explained. “Don't make them feel bad for prioritising themselves and their needs. It will potentially, you know, make them feel worse long-term. I just honour that everyone needs to do what's best for them, whether financially, emotionally, or physically.”

Questions 12–18

12. According to the text, the majority of people in the USA plan to … on Thanksgiving.

Ответ: 2. spend time with relatives
Логика: Первое предложение говорит, что большинство уже определилось с семейными планами; далее названы “hosting a big meal” и “heading to a relative’s house”. Это вариант 2.

13. The statistics mentioned in paragraph 2 prove that …

Ответ: 3. loneliness increased partly because of the pandemic
Логика: Текст прямо говорит, что 70% сталкивались с разными видами одиночества перед праздниками, “partly due to the effects of the Covid-19 pandemic”. Это вариант 3.

14. How does the therapist Lilia Magon explain feeling lonely at Thanksgiving?

Ответ: 1. The traditional image of the holiday is family-related
Логика: Магон связывает переживания с ожиданиями от праздника и отношений: “unmet expectations of what you think a holiday is supposed to look like”. Вариант 1 обобщает мысль о привычном образе семейного праздника.

15. Which is NOT mentioned in paragraphs 6–7 as a way to fight loneliness during the holiday season?

Ответ: 2. Following family traditions
Логика: В тексте есть совет обратиться к therapist или trusted friend и “reframe” праздник. Следование семейным традициям как способ борьбы с одиночеством не предлагается.

16. The word “animosity” is closest in meaning to …

Ответ: 2. unfriendliness
Логика: В контексте речь о болезненных чувствах к людям, которые причинили боль. “Unfriendliness” — самый близкий из предложенных вариантов.

17. In “that it’s going to be a hard time for you”, “it” most probably refers to …

Ответ: 3. holiday
Логика: Предыдущие предложения говорят о том, как человек хочет провести “these days” и создать свои traditions; “it” относится к предстоящему праздничному периоду.

18. What is the main idea of the text?

Ответ: 4. There should be no pressure to celebrate holidays in certain ways
Логика: Финал призывает уважать решение человека и не заставлять его праздновать определённым образом: “respect that choice” и “do what’s best for them”. Это вариант 4.

Variant 3 · Changes in work culture

Поколение Z и изменения в рабочей культуре · источник: загруженный сборник, PDF: стр. 31–32

Work culture is changing thanks to Generation Z, defined as “the youngest generation with adult members (born 1997 to 2013)”. The misconceptions created by older generations should change, too. The stereotype that the younger generation is lazy is not only untrue, but ignores the necessary changes they are bringing to work culture.

Older generations have labeled Gen Z as lazy, selfish, and uncaring. One reason older generations stereotype the younger one as lazy is because of the notion that young people don’t want to work. This on its own is a myth and outrageously wrong. The priorities of Generation Z are just different from other generations’ priorities.

These stereotypes are born out of the fact that work culture is changing, but it’s for the better. This low work ethic concept is mistaken because much of Generation Z doesn’t want to settle for traditional 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. office jobs. Older generations have their own set of norms of what work culture should look like, but what these older generations overlook is that just because a job isn’t central doesn’t mean it is not hard work.

According to some statistics, members of Generation Z are an “intensely entrepreneurial generation, with almost two-thirds, 62 percent, either having started or wanting to start their own businesses”. They prioritize a work-life balance that has never been “business as usual” for other generations. What is misunderstood by older generations is that because Generation Z doesn’t want to work traditional 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. jobs, they just don’t want to work at all. That is simply not true.

Katie Milliams is the chief executive and founder of a company helping organizations unlock performance and engagement by reimagining how, when and where work is done. She said when younger workers talk about balance, they are saying they will work hard but also need a life. “What they are saying is, ‘I will work hard for you, but I also need a life,’” Milliams said in the interview. “Unfortunately, what leaders hear is, ‘I want to work less.’”

Remote or hybrid jobs are much more common than they used to be before the COVID-19 pandemic. These positions may seem less intense for other generations, but Generation Z works smarter, not harder, and that might be too difficult for some to fathom. If you can get your job done at home, where you feel most comfortable, on your own time, while still having an outside life, why wouldn’t you?

Generation Z has been falsely blamed for redefining what a job can look and be: business casual attire, remote workplaces, and even flexible schedules where they can choose their own hours. It is even argued that they are actually saving everyone’s work-life balance.

According to an interview with Eva Delio, the executive vice president of recruiting at a famous cloud-based software company, Generation Z has “proven the world that you don’t need to be in the office nine to five to be efficient. This generation is single-handedly paving the way for the entire workforce to do their jobs remotely.” Generation Z has watched previous generations struggle with work-life balance, time off, and being overworked. Demanding change may seem as if they are avoiding work, but surveys show older generations secretly want more flexibility, too.

There is nothing wrong with change, especially when the type of change is good for everyone. For way too long, work has been people’s largest passion. People spend so much time and energy, but it shouldn’t have to be that way. It’s not all about work, and flexibility in the workplace is the key to a healthy life.

Открыть оригинальную страницу сборника (текст)

Questions 12–18

12. The author thinks that Generation Z is …

Ответ: 4. mistakenly defined by many
Логика: В начале текста говорится о misconceptions и стереотипе, что молодые люди ленивы: “The stereotype ... is not only untrue”. Автор считает, что поколение неверно понимают/описывают.

13. Which is NOT true about the attitude to work, according to the text?

Ответ: 4. Generation Z avoids hard work because they are selfish
Логика: Автор прямо называет стереотип о лени мифом и говорит, что изменение приоритетов не означает нежелание работать. Поэтому вариант 4 противоречит тексту.

14. The phrasal verb “settle for” is closest in meaning to …

Ответ: 4. accept
Логика: В выражении “doesn’t want to settle for traditional ... jobs” значение — согласиться на / принять как достаточное. Подходит accept.

15. The statistics given in the text prove that compared to older generations, people from Generation Z …

Ответ: 1. start businesses on their own
Логика: В тексте сказано, что 62% уже начали или хотят начать собственный бизнес. Это напрямую соответствует варианту 1.

16. The quote by the chief executive Katie Milliams is given to …

Ответ: 3. emphasize the gap between Gen Z and their chiefs
Логика: Контраст прямой: молодые говорят “I will work hard ... but I also need a life”, а руководители слышат “I want to work less”. Цитата показывает разрыв в интерпретации слов.

17. What is the author's position on remote work expressed in paragraphs 6 and 7?

Ответ: 2. It provides more flexibility and can be equally effective
Логика: Автор пишет, что можно выполнить работу дома, в комфортных условиях и в собственное время; цитата подчёркивает, что не обязательно находиться в офисе 9–5, чтобы быть efficient. Это вариант 2.

18. What is the main idea of the text?

Ответ: 3. The younger generation is changing our attitude to work
Логика: В тексте повторяется идея, что Gen Z меняет представления о рабочем графике, удалённой работе и балансе. Вариант 3 наиболее полно охватывает главную мысль.

Общий алгоритм разбора

  1. Определи тип вопроса: главная мысль, конкретная информация, значение слова, местоименная ссылка или NOT mentioned/NOT true.
  2. Найди в тексте не обязательно те же слова, а смысловой эквивалент: в ЕГЭ часто используется paraphrase.
  3. Подчеркни доказательство. Для вопроса NOT/NOT true проверь каждый вариант: три подтверждаются или упоминаются, один — нет либо противоречит тексту.
  4. Не выбирай вариант только потому, что в нём есть знакомое слово. Ответ должен подтверждаться всем контекстом.
06 · HOMEWORK

Домашняя работа · 10 заданий в день

В заданиях смешиваются только времена, которые прошли к концу этого урока: Present Simple, Present Continuous, Past Simple, Past Continuous, Future Simple, Present Perfect, Present Perfect Continuous, Past Perfect и Future Continuous.

Day 1 · Choose the correct tense

  1. She usually ___ (work) from home, but this week she ___ (work) from the office.
  2. I ___ (not / finish) the book yet.
  3. At 10 last night, they ___ (watch) a documentary.
  4. By the time we reached the cinema, the film ___ already ___ (start).
  5. This time tomorrow, I ___ (sit) on the plane.
  6. He ___ (learn) English for three years, and he still takes lessons.
  7. Look! The dog ___ (run) towards the gate.
  8. Last summer, we ___ (visit) three different cities.
  9. “I’m cold.” — “I ___ (close) the window.”
  10. ___ you ever ___ (try) surfing?
Ответы: 1 works; is working. 2 haven’t finished. 3 were watching. 4 had; started. 5 will be sitting. 6 has been learning. 7 is running. 8 visited. 9 will close. 10 Have; tried.

Day 2 · Build the form

  1. Make negative: She has been waiting for an hour.
  2. Make a question: They had left before noon.
  3. Make negative: I will be using the computer at 6.
  4. Make a question: He works on Saturdays.
  5. Make negative: We were discussing the plan.
  6. Make a question: You have seen this film.
  7. Make negative: She called me yesterday.
  8. Make a question: They will help us.
  9. Make negative: He had checked the details.
  10. Make a question: You are studying now.
Ответы: 1 She hasn’t been waiting for an hour. 2 Had they left before noon? 3 I won’t be using the computer at 6. 4 Does he work on Saturdays? 5 We weren’t discussing the plan. 6 Have you seen this film? 7 She didn’t call me yesterday. 8 Will they help us? 9 He hadn’t checked the details. 10 Are you studying now?

Day 3 · Mixed tenses in context

  1. While I ___ (walk) home, I ___ (meet) an old friend.
  2. She ___ (not / answer) yet, so I’ll call her later.
  3. By the time the guests arrived, we ___ (prepare) everything.
  4. They ___ (discuss) the problem for two hours and need a break.
  5. This time next month, we ___ (live) in a different city.
  6. My brother never ___ (drink) coffee in the evening.
  7. At the moment, the students ___ (work) on a difficult task.
  8. We ___ (not / know) about the change until yesterday.
  9. When I entered the room, everyone ___ (talk).
  10. Don’t worry, I ___ (send) you the link tonight.
Ответы: 1 was walking; met. 2 hasn’t answered. 3 had prepared. 4 have been discussing. 5 will be living. 6 drinks. 7 are working. 8 didn’t know. 9 was talking / were talking (согласовать с субъектом everyone → was talking). 10 will send.

Day 4 · Exam-style control

  1. By the time the teacher came in, the students ___ (complete) the first task.
  2. She ___ (work) on the report since 9 a.m., and she is still not finished.
  3. This time tomorrow, we ___ (take) our English test.
  4. He ___ never ___ (see) snow before he moved to Canada.
  5. While they ___ (wait) for the bus, it started to rain.
  6. I ___ (not / hear) this song before. Is it new?
  7. What ___ you ___ (do) at 8 p.m. yesterday?
  8. Our teacher usually ___ (give) us feedback after each test.
  9. “Someone’s at the door.” — “I ___ (open) it.”
  10. Choose the tense and explain: “She had already left when I arrived.” Identify which action happened first and quote the word(s) that help you understand the order.
Ответы: 1 had completed. 2 has been working. 3 will be taking. 4 had; seen. 5 were waiting. 6 haven’t heard. 7 were; doing. 8 gives. 9 will open. 10 Past Perfect: she left first; “had already left” marks the earlier past action, and “when I arrived” is the later event.

Vocabulary box · повторение

Выбери 8–10 слов из reading-блоков. Для каждого запиши перевод, короткое словосочетание и собственный пример. На следующем уроке нужно будет вспомнить их без подсказки.

Цель урока

Не просто узнать формулы новых времён, а научиться выбирать форму по ситуации, доказывать ответ контекстом и постепенно наращивать словарь для чтения ЕГЭ.

Открой, чтобы увидеть ключи и пояснения преподавателя.
